newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-DE GLANVILLE SUFFERS LIONS REJECTION.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-DE GLANVILLE SUFFERS LIONS REJECTION.

text.p: England captain Phil de Glanville and compatriots Tony Underwood and Jon Sleightholme have been left out of the initial 62-man British Lions training squad for this year's tour of South Africa.
Twenty-seven Englishmen were named on Monday to attend a training session in Birmingham next month, with the final squad of 35 being announced on April 2.
But with de Glanville ignored and Will Carling unavailable, none of the three-quarter line involved in England's record 46-6 win over Ireland on Saturday have been chosen.

Instead, four English scrum-halves have been named -- Andy Gomarsall, Kyran Bracken, Austin Healey and Matt Dawson -- along with three uncapped players, Will Greenwood, Jim Mallinder and Martin Corry.
There are also six former rugby league players, headed by Scott Gibbs and Scott Quinnell who are among 13 Welshmen nominated.
Thirteen Irishmen and a mere nine Scots complete the squad, although manager Fran Cotton insists there is still time for other contenders to force their way in.
The captaincy issue remains unresolved, with increasing calls for a test skipper to be named only once the team have arrived in South Africa.

Scotland's Rob Wainwright was the pre-Five Nations favourite but Scotland's poor start and competition for back-row places has increased support for England's Jason Leonard and Martin Johnson, with Ireland's Keith Wood a contender if he recovers from shoulder problems.
